questions.prompt: In the Book of Mormon narrative, who abridged the large plates of Nephi into most of the Book of Mormon?
questions.explanation: Narrative reading: Mormon abridged centuries of Nephite records onto the plates that bear his name; his son Moroni finished them.

questions.prompt: In the Book of Mormon narrative, which of these happened first?
options: Captain Moroni raises the title of liberty
Samuel the Lamanite prophesies from the wall
King Benjamin gives his final address
questions.explanation: Narrative reading: King Benjamin's address comes about 124 BC — roughly fifty years before the title of liberty and more than a century before Samuel.

questions.prompt: In the Book of Mormon narrative, where did Alma baptize those who believed Abinadi's words?
questions.explanation: Narrative reading: Alma gathered believers in secret at the Waters of Mormon, where about 204 were baptized.

questions.prompt: In the Book of Mormon narrative, roughly when did Lehi's family leave Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The Book of Mormon’s chronology places the departure about 600 BCE. Its identification of Zedekiah’s first regnal year creates a chronological difficulty: conventional historical dating places his accession in 597 BCE. Do not treat these dates as reconciled.

questions.prompt: In the Book of Mormon narrative, the resurrected Christ first appeared to the Nephites at the temple in which land?
questions.explanation: Narrative reading: A multitude gathered around the temple in the land Bountiful when they heard the Father's voice introduce His Son.

questions.prompt: In the Book of Mormon narrative, in Alma 32, Alma compares the word of God to what?
questions.explanation: Narrative reading: Alma invites his listeners to plant the word like a seed and watch whether it swells, sprouts and grows.

questions.prompt: In the Book of Mormon narrative, who was Alma teaching in Alma 32?
options: The humble poor among the Zoramites
questions.explanation: Narrative reading: The poor had been cast out of the Zoramite synagogues, and Alma taught them that humility prepared them to receive the word.

questions.prompt: In the Book of Mormon narrative, according to Alma 32:27, what is enough to begin the experiment upon the word?
questions.explanation: Narrative reading: Alma says that if they can no more than desire to believe, they should let that desire work in them.

questions.prompt: Which empire conquered the northern kingdom of Israel in 722 BC?
questions.explanation: Assyria took Samaria and carried the northern tribes away; Judah fell to Babylon more than a century later, in 587 BC.

questions.prompt: According to 1 Kings 6, who built the first temple in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: David prepared for it, but his son Solomon built the temple; Zerubbabel led the rebuilding after the exile.

questions.prompt: In James 1:5, what should someone who lacks wisdom do?
questions.explanation: Scriptural reading: James directs the reader to ask God. LDS seminary applies this passage to acquiring spiritual knowledge.

questions.prompt: What does Genesis 1:26–27 say about humanity?
questions.explanation: Scriptural reading: the passage describes humanity in relation to God’s image. Traditions interpret that relationship differently.

questions.prompt: Which pair of commandments does Matthew 22:36–39 emphasize?
questions.explanation: Scriptural reading: Jesus joins love of God with love of neighbor.

questions.prompt: In Mosiah 2:17, serving other people is also described as what?
questions.explanation: LDS scriptural reading: Benjamin connects service to others with service to God.

questions.prompt: What two approaches to learning are joined in D&C 88:118?
questions.explanation: LDS scriptural reading: the revelation commends both study and faith.

questions.prompt: Which source explicitly teaches the LDS understanding of the Father’s embodied nature?
questions.explanation: LDS doctrine: this revelation describes the Father and Son as embodied. Nicene traditions use a different account of divine being.

questions.prompt: Which modern American geography does the LDS Church officially endorse for Book of Mormon events?
questions.explanation: LDS institutional position: specific American locations are not endorsed. Geographic proposals must remain labeled as proposals.

questions.prompt: In Moroni 10, who addresses future readers of the record?
questions.explanation: Narrative reading: Moroni addresses later readers and invites them to ask God about the record.

questions.prompt: In Genesis 12:10, where does Abram go because of famine?
questions.explanation: Biblical narrative: Abram travels to Egypt. This answer identifies the setting in the text, not a reconstructed itinerary.

questions.prompt: In 2 Kings 25, which power captures Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Biblical narrative: the text depicts the Babylonian conquest and deportation.

questions.prompt: In Mark 1:16, Jesus encounters Simon and Andrew beside which body of water?
questions.explanation: Gospel narrative: the encounter takes place beside the Sea of Galilee.

questions.prompt: Which island is named after the shipwreck in Acts 28:1?
questions.explanation: Narrative geography: the KJV calls the island Melita, conventionally identified with Malta.

questions.prompt: Which distinction matters when evaluating a historical account?
options: Event date versus date the account was recorded
Paper color versus font size only
questions.explanation: Historical method: an account written later can describe an earlier event. The First Vision documents illustrate why these dates must be recorded separately.

questions.prompt: How does the Israel Antiquities Authority describe biblical Dead Sea Scroll manuscripts?
options: All are identical to a modern printed Bible
Some closely resemble the Masoretic Text; others differ
questions.explanation: Manuscript evidence: the collection preserves both textual continuity and variant readings.

questions.prompt: What does the University of Münster’s Institute for New Testament Textual Research investigate?
options: The transmission history of the Greek New Testament
questions.explanation: Academic method: the institute studies Greek manuscript transmission and prepares critical editions. Reconstructing textual history is a different question from evaluating divine inspiration.

questions.prompt: According to the Joseph Smith Papers, when was the earliest surviving firsthand First Vision account recorded?
questions.explanation: Documentary history: the 1832 account records an earlier reported experience. Its recording date is not the claimed event date.

questions.prompt: In Didache 7, what alternative is allowed if suitable baptismal water is unavailable?
options: Pouring water on the head three times
questions.explanation: Primary-text reading: this instruction allows pouring as an alternative. One community text does not establish uniform practice everywhere.

questions.prompt: In First Apology 67, which activity is part of the gathering Justin describes?
options: Reading apostolic memoirs and prophetic writings
questions.explanation: Primary-text reading: Justin describes readings, exhortation and communal worship in his defense of Christians.

questions.prompt: What does Irenaeus appeal to in Against Heresies III.3?
questions.explanation: Primary-text reading: Irenaeus uses succession to argue against rival teachings. Later traditions evaluate this argument differently.

questions.prompt: What kind of text is the Martyrdom of Polycarp?
questions.explanation: Genre: the narrative commemorates a Christian martyr. Its religious and literary purposes belong in historical evaluation.

questions.prompt: Which council came first?
questions.explanation: Historical chronology: Nicaea preceded Constantinople and Chalcedon. Theological judgments about councils differ among traditions.

questions.prompt: How should an app present a universal loss of priesthood authority followed by restoration?
options: As a conclusion shared by every historian
As a date proved by a map
As an LDS theological claim, with other traditions’ views identified
questions.explanation: Comparative theology: LDS restoration claims differ from Catholic and Orthodox accounts of continuity. Historical documentation alone does not resolve divine authority.

questions.prompt: How does the Catholic Catechism describe the Trinity?
options: One person with three temporary names
One God in three distinct persons
questions.explanation: Catholic self-description: unity of divine being and distinction of persons are both affirmed.

questions.prompt: In the Orthodox creed linked here, the Holy Spirit proceeds from whom?
questions.explanation: Orthodox self-description: this wording differs from the Latin filioque formulation. Use each tradition’s own formulation.

questions.prompt: What organization date is recorded in D&C 20:1?
questions.explanation: LDS canonical source: section 20 identifies April 6, 1830 as the organization date.

questions.prompt: Which section is the Kirtland Temple dedicatory prayer?
questions.explanation: LDS canonical source: section 109 contains the dedicatory prayer.

questions.prompt: Which passage describes influence through persuasion and gentleness?
questions.explanation: LDS scriptural reading: the passage describes persuasion, patience and gentleness as principles of priesthood influence.

questions.prompt: Which source directly addresses plural marriage in Kirtland and Nauvoo?
options: The Gospel Topics Essay of that title
questions.explanation: LDS institutional historical interpretation: read the essay alongside section 132 and the documents cited in its notes.

questions.prompt: Which section gives instructions for the westward migration?
questions.explanation: LDS canonical source: section 136 addresses the organization and conduct of the migrating camps.

questions.prompt: Which statement best matches the Church’s essay about the 1890 Manifesto?
options: Every plural marriage ended immediately in 1890
Ending plural marriage was a process extending beyond 1890
questions.explanation: Documented history in an LDS official essay: some new plural marriages continued after 1890; later measures enforced cessation.

questions.prompt: What did the 1978 change described in Official Declaration 2 address?
options: Priesthood and temple restrictions affecting Black members
questions.explanation: LDS historical account: the change removed race-based priesthood and temple restrictions. The Church now rejects earlier racial explanations.

questions.prompt: Which narrative connects Israel’s covenant with Sinai?
questions.explanation: Hebrew Bible narrative: Exodus 19 sets the covenant encounter at Sinai. Later Jewish and Christian interpretations differ.

questions.prompt: Which passage connects Moses’ call with the divine name?
questions.explanation: Hebrew Bible reading: the passage connects the divine self-identification with Moses’ commission. Translation and interpretation require care.

questions.prompt: Which chapter gathers instructions for Israel’s appointed festivals?
questions.explanation: Hebrew Bible reading: the chapter describes sacred occasions and their observance. Modern Jewish practice has its own subsequent history.
